prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/brand.tsx. The documented product design system intentionally uses purple and indigo brand tokens. The surface has no other generic-default cluster. Preserve that brand decision while checking the rest of the UI for unmotivated defaults.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/onboarding.tsx. The UI labels three real ordered onboarding steps as 01 CONNECT ACCOUNT, 02 CHOOSE SOURCES, and 03 FINISH. Keep the real sequence, but remove decorative numbered scaffolding elsewhere if it has no sequential meaning.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/home.tsx. The page combines an unexplained purple gradient, generic Inter typography, large rounded surfaces, and decorative 01 section kickers. No project, brand, task, or reference evidence explains those choices. Review the combination without treating any one choice as forbidden.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/journal.tsx. The page uses cream surfaces, Instrument Serif, and sage or forest-green accents with no established brand or product reason. Check whether this is a replacement anti-slop default rather than automatically approving it because it avoids purple SaaS styling.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/home.tsx. The route is running in a browser that supports read-only JavaScript evaluation. The source gate is inconclusive about whether the rendered page is a centered mega-hero followed by exactly three equal feature cards and repeated 01/02/03 kickers. Use rendered evidence without mutating the page, then adjudicate the result against the product role and selected direction.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/settings.tsx. Browser screenshots are available at desktop and mobile widths, but the browser tool cannot execute page JavaScript. Finish the visual verification without inventing DOM measurements.
scenario: The optional rendered structural detector degrades cleanly when JavaScript evaluation is unavailable; existing rendered evidence remains authoritative.

prompt: redesign-existing deep the dashboard, settings, and audit-log routes as one coordinated product pass. Their first-screen jobs and content priorities differ, but the current rendered routes appear to reuse the same hero-plus-repeated-cards macro skeleton. Browser read-only evaluation is available. Compare the in-scope routes at matching viewports and review whether the repeated macrostructure is an intentional shared system or unmotivated reuse.
scenario: Systemic multi-route design work can compare rendered macro fingerprints to catch repeated default skeletons that per-route checks cannot establish.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/settings.tsx. Browser read-only evaluation is available. Review and improve this one route only; no other product surface is in scope.
scenario: Cross-surface macro comparison is conditional and must not expand a bounded single-route task.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/library.tsx. The documented product design system intentionally uses 24px media-card radii and a consistent rounded icon-container motif for content types. Browser read-only evaluation is available. Preserve that owned system while checking whether the rendered density turns into generic over-round or icon-tile decoration elsewhere.
scenario: Rendered radius and icon-density measurements remain contextual when an explicit product system owns the same geometry.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/admin.tsx. The rendered surface has six large 28px rounded cards, generic rounded icon tiles on most cards, icons across nearly every content block, and one section of three equal feature cards. No project, brand, task, or reference evidence explains those choices. Use browser evidence to review the combined defaults without treating radius or icons as forbidden alone.
scenario: A rendered chrome-density cluster can strengthen review when several independent defaults co-occur, while each individual style remains valid in context.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/docs-home.tsx. The product IA intentionally uses a five-link top navigation with one Get Started action, a four-column documentation footer, and one primary/secondary hero action pair. Browser read-only evaluation is available. Preserve that documented IA and action hierarchy while checking whether similar shell patterns repeat elsewhere on this surface without a content reason.
scenario: Familiar nav/footer/CTA geometry remains valid when it follows explicit information architecture and real action hierarchy.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/home.tsx. The rendered page has a wide nav with five plain links plus one filled CTA, a four-column footer, repeated filled-primary plus outline-secondary CTA pairs in three sections, and exactly three equal feature cards. No project, IA, task, or reference evidence explains the combination. Review the combined shell defaults without banning any one familiar pattern alone.
scenario: Several weak rendered shell defaults become stronger evidence only when they co-occur with an independent structural default.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/pricing.tsx. This is an explicit commercial pricing page: the product brief requires plan comparison, an FAQ, and a final signup action after the plan section. Browser read-only evaluation is available. Review the rendered page for a SaaS meta-template, but preserve the required product story and do not treat the presence of pricing plus FAQ as a failure by itself.
scenario: A real pricing page can legitimately contain pricing, FAQ, and closing action; G63 is about an inherited whole-page sequence rather than forbidding commercial content.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/home.tsx. The rendered page uses a centered hero, exactly three equal feature cards, a pricing section, an FAQ section, a closing CTA block, the generic wide nav pattern, and a four-column footer. No project, product-story, IA, or reference evidence explains this sequence. Review the combined defaults as a possible SaaS meta-template without claiming AI authorship.
scenario: A full inherited SaaS sequence becomes stronger evidence when it co-occurs with independent generic shell families, while each constituent section remains valid when product-required.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/catalog.tsx. Browser read-only evaluation is available. Preserve that documented system while checking whether rendered elevation or rhythm becomes unmotivated elsewhere.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/home.tsx. The rendered page has six rounded cards where four use both borders and large soft shadows, six top-level sections with nearly identical spacing, exactly three equal feature cards, and large radii across most cards. No project, brand, task, or reference evidence explains the combination. Review the combined defaults without treating shadows, borders, radii, or regular spacing as forbidden alone.
scenario: Weak rendered elevation and rhythm defaults strengthen a review only when they co-occur with stronger independent structural choices.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/subscriptions.tsx. Each subscription card intentionally needs a provider icon, plan tags, monthly price, billing status, and a management action because those are distinct operational facts. Browser read-only evaluation is available. Preserve the task-required card facets while checking whether additional decorative density creates a kitchen-sink card.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/home.tsx. The rendered page has three equal large-radius cards; at least two cards each combine decorative iconography, multiple rounded tags, a price-like label, status chrome, and a CTA even though the cards only need a title and short description. prompt: improve the rendered anti-slop detector because G31 is producing too many false positives on our card-heavy product. Do not just loosen the radius threshold from this anecdote; calibrate the change against existing positive and boundary-negative rendered cases and preserve contextual project authority.
scenario: Rendered heuristic tuning must be calibration-driven rather than reactively weakened from one false-positive report.

prompt: extend the rendered anti-slop detector with a new contextual visual signal. Add the detector only if the same change also supplies deterministic positive and boundary-negative calibration fixtures, keeps the signal contextual, and proves the fixture matrix covers every active rendered rule.
scenario: Every future rendered detector must ship with explicit calibration coverage so thresholds cannot silently drift.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/home.tsx. Source taste-gate and rendered taste-gate both flag G31 surface-radius on the same candidate. Fuse the reports before judging the cluster so the same semantic family is counted once, not twice.
scenario: Source and rendered evidence for the same semantic decision must corroborate rather than inflate cluster scoring.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/home.tsx. Source evidence has an unexplained purple-gradient family worth 2; rendered evidence has exactly-three cards worth 2 and over-round worth 1. No individual channel reaches the cluster threshold. Fuse the independent families, preserve any source hard gate unchanged, and treat a fused cluster as contextual rendered evidence rather than an automatic failure.
scenario: Independent source and rendered families can jointly cross the calibrated review threshold without weakening source hard gates or turning render heuristics into blockers.

prompt: improve-existing standard /src/routes/settings.tsx. Browser JavaScript evaluation is unavailable, but I still need the final anti-slop mechanical evidence receipt. Run the source evidence path, do not fabricate rendered DOM metrics, and make the receipt explicitly say rendered evidence was not measured rather than implying a visual pass.

prompt: improve-existing deep the two in-scope rendered routes /src/routes/home.tsx and /src/routes/pricing.tsx. Source and per-route rendered evidence are available and a cross-surface G02 comparator report already exists. Produce one final mechanical receipt using an explicit multi-candidate manifest: bind each source target to its declared route and exact snapshot before fusion, require the cross-surface report to cover that same rendered candidate set exactly, preserve source hard gates, and keep G02 separate from the fused score.
scenario: The final multi-route receipt binds each source/render pair explicitly and accepts cross-surface evidence only for the exact same rendered candidate set, without collapsing lane semantics or claiming mechanical evidence is the final visual verdict.

prompt: improve the source anti-slop detector because one contextual source rule is producing false positives. Do not tune the rule from that one anecdote. Preserve source hard-gate behavior, update deterministic positive and boundary-negative calibration evidence for the affected source rule, and keep detector behavior contextual where the registry says it is contextual.
scenario: Source detector maintenance is calibration-driven just like rendered detector maintenance; one false-positive report cannot silently weaken the registry.

prompt: extend the anti-slop signal registry with a new contextual rule whose evidence cites local policy and an external field guide. Keep the provenance machine-checkable: every evidence source ID used by the rule must resolve in the registry source catalog, and the new source rule must ship with positive and boundary-negative source calibration before qualification.
scenario: Registry provenance and source calibration are release contracts, preventing orphan source IDs and uncalibrated detector growth.

prompt: improve-existing standard a 360px browser-extension popup. Keep its purpose, content, and controls, but make it feel like a native browser utility instead of a miniature SaaS dashboard. prompt: improve-existing standard src/routes/production.tsx. The rendered production dashboard has four equally prominent KPI tiles even though only one is actionable, a table led by raw machine IDs, tiny labels next to expansive blank space, and conflicting 'QA passed', 'in progress', and 'ready to publish' language while authorization is not confirmed. Preserve real functionality and known product contracts. Treat the browser screenshots as evidence; check the underlying states before asserting a contradiction. Review task-first acceptance even when the taste source scan is green.
scenario: Operator dashboard regression: a non-purple, non-gradient card-wall can still fail the user's task. The skill checks product-priority, legibility, status truth, and card purpose against rendered evidence without inventing data or blindly rewriting IA.

prompt: improve-existing standard src/routes/metrics.tsx. A read-only operations console has four equally sized verified metrics because the user must compare the same measure across four regions. The dense settings and shared shell are intentional, all values are sourced, and normal-zoom text is legible. Keep the valid comparison structure unless a concrete task-first defect is observed; do not force asymmetry or invent video thumbnails just to avoid AI slop.
scenario: Counterexample regression: valid repeated metric cards and a dense operator shell remain permitted when they serve a real comparison task, rather than triggering a blanket anti-card rule.

prompt: improve-existing standard src/routes/production.tsx. The previous version was a generic dark card dashboard. A new warm paper-like design removes most cards, but applies hairline dividers, tracked monospace micro-labels, and the same editorial row treatment to the job queue, app setup steps, settings form, video preview, and explanatory prose. The palette is coherent and the source taste gate reports green. Review the rendered desktop and mobile screens: do not merely swap to a third style preset, and do not equate removing cards with completing the UX fix.
scenario: Regression from real design iteration: replacing a dark SaaS card-wall with a light editorial divider-wall is not automatically improved role distribution. Inspect the render, allocate style by semantic component job, and repair unearned sameness without repainting the product again.

prompt: improve-existing standard src/routes/audit-log.tsx. The UI is a dense evidence ledger with repeated hairline row separators, monospace timestamps, and consistent per-row status markers. These are comparable chronological records, and the visual design has readable text, proper accessible state, and obvious filtering. Preserve the intentional repeated ledger grammar. Do not force asymmetric cards, colorful panels, or irregular divider patterns only to make it look less AI generated.
scenario: Boundary negative: repeated ledger separators and monospace metadata are valid for genuinely comparable rows. The style allocation check must avoid artificial asymmetry or bans on beige, rules, or monospace.

prompt: build-product-surface standard a local video-production workspace with an actionable queue, a publishing-authorization setup flow, a settings form, and a rendered-video preview. The chosen brand direction is clean monochrome with blue accents. Keep product facts and accessibility contracts. Before implementation, decide which content roles share a visual grammar and which need a differentiated interaction hierarchy; do not make every region a ruled list. The resulting render looks consistent but essential form labels and upload blockers are hard to find.
scenario: Greenfield boundary: a selected monochrome visual world is legitimate, but functional failures and an undifferentiated interface must be repaired without abandoning the art direction or fabricating product data.

prompt: improve-existing standard these three existing routes: /jobs, /tiktok-setup, and /settings. The previous audit found that the job queue is buried (UX-01), the setup screen hides the next action (UX-02), and settings offer no context for crop controls (UX-03). The new desktop screenshots show that the queue was moved above the library, while the setup guide and settings remain essentially unchanged. The style scan is green. Continue the design iteration: compare what was actually resolved and carry the other findings forward instead of claiming the product redesign is complete.
scenario: Cross-route incomplete progress: one dashboard improvement does not close previously known setup and settings issues. The verification receipt must preserve issue IDs and surface coverage even when the mechanical style gate is green.

prompt: improve-existing standard src/routes/settings.tsx. The user requests another visual iteration but the current settings form groups related controls correctly, reads comfortably at normal zoom and matches the approved design system. Compare it with the earlier screenshot. No concrete defect is found. Do not change the layout only to show progress; leave the settings page unchanged with a justified review result.
scenario: Positive control: evidence-backed KEEP_JUSTIFIED for an adequate screen is a legitimate outcome. The design process must not introduce changes merely to produce a visibly different screenshot.

prompt: audit-surface standard src/routes/queue.tsx. The only old screenshot is an empty queue at 1440x900 desktop, while the only new screenshot is a populated queue at 375px mobile width. Source code changed and the visual scanner passes. Assess whether queue readability improved, but do not claim a measured before/after improvement from these unmatched captures. The app cannot be run in this environment.
scenario: Unmatched viewport and state cannot support a comparative usability claim. A read-only audit reports observations and gaps rather than fabricating matched evidence.

prompt: build-product-surface standard a new inventory management editor. No earlier UI exists. Render the first representative candidate, record that the primary save action is hard to locate and the recovery state is unclear, then implement a revision. Use that first candidate as the baseline, verify each acceptance condition on the new render, and keep unresolved cases open. Do not invent an old screenshot.
scenario: Greenfield exception: no historical before UI is required; use the first real rendered candidate as the baseline for all subsequent iterations.

prompt: improve-existing standard src/routes/publishing.tsx. The design revision makes the queue action more prominent but also introduces a publish button that appears enabled when TikTok authorization is missing. Desktop screenshots confirm the visual affordance, but API behavior has not been exercised. The style and lint gates are green. Evaluate the outcome, note the new regression, and do not claim functionality or final readiness from screenshot appearance alone.
scenario: A successful visual iteration can introduce a new authorization affordance defect. Track that regression separately and prevent CI green or style polish from promoting the result to complete.

prompt: audit-surface standard src/pages/Jobs.tsx. The production UI has a clickable row 'All → Script → Voice → Cut → Render → QA → Publish → Failed'. Selecting a chip filters the job queue; QA passed (3), Publish (0), Failed (0). The UI calls this a pipeline progress rail. All three jobs have completed QA, but TikTok authorization is missing. Read the source state and selectors before recommending changes. Explain which labels are current phases, historical outcomes, filter selections, and publishing eligibility, and whether failed belongs on the chronological path. Do not assume Publish means published or ready without a contract.
scenario: Mixed stage rail regression: progress metaphor, filters, historical QA and publish eligibility are different concepts. The skill must source the meaning rather than trusting the attractive sequence.

prompt: improve-existing standard src/routes/work-items.tsx. A filter row shows All 3, QA 3, Published 1, Failed 1. Jobs can have QA passed and be published, and a previously failed attempt can be retried successfully. The backend selectors intentionally compute overlapping milestone counts, not disjoint current-phase buckets. A designer complains that the counts do not sum to three and wants to rewrite the state machine to make them mutually exclusive. Preserve the correct semantics, but assess whether the interface explains the overlap and its filtering.
scenario: Counterexample: status categories may overlap. Counts need not sum to All unless the data contract says the categories are disjoint.

prompt: improve-existing standard src/pages/Pipeline.tsx. Clicking 'Render 4' selects a view filter, but keyboard focus is lost and the 4 shown items include only 3 matching records after a separate search term is applied. The filter chip looks like the currently executing phase, even though it is only a query. The product already has correct backend state data. Update only the UI behavior, labeling and count/filter scope, and verify with representative keyboard, empty-state and search-filter interactions; do not change job lifecycle states.
scenario: A stage-looking UI is actually an accessible filtering surface. Check compound filter counts, keyboard state and empty results without modifying the backend lifecycle.

prompt: audit-surface standard src/pages/JobDetail.tsx. The screenshot shows a green QA PASSED result and a blue 'Publish to TikTok' button, but the connected-account state, API permission checks and action handler are not available for inspection. Another screenshot of the setup page says account not connected. Determine whether publishing readiness is verified. Do not claim the button is definitely functional or broken merely from a screenshot.
scenario: Read-only screenshot critique: visual affordance concerns can be documented without claiming runtime behavior or inventing provider authorization rules.

prompt: build-product-surface standard a local document-processing workbench with a stage timeline, concurrent translation and validation tasks, a review outcome, an 'Errors' filter, and a gated 'Export' action requiring completed checks and user permission. Work stages are not mutually exclusive, errors may be retried. Create a genuine task-oriented UI, define the semantics matrix before treating the timeline as a stepper, and demonstrate state-dependent export and filtering without imposing a single linear state machine.
scenario: Greenfield control: stages can be concurrent or optional. The skill must faithfully map task semantics instead of forcing every product into a linear pipeline.
